questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Departmental Undertakings' refers to.
questions.a: Departmental undertakings are the oldest and most traditional form of public enterprise where a government department is directly run by a ministry, financed by annual appropriations from the treasury, and subject to the same accounting, audit and budgeting rules as other government activities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Departmental Undertakings'.
questions.a: These enterprises are an extension of the government itself, with no separate legal identity, and their employees are civil servants subject to government rules.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Departmental Undertakings' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Forms of Public Sector Enterprises

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Statutory Corporations' refers to.
questions.a: A statutory corporation is a body corporate created by a special Act of Parliament or a state legislature, owned by the government, financed by its own resources, and having the power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract in its own name.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Statutory Corporations'.
questions.a: It enjoys a separate legal identity from the government, is governed by the provisions of its founding Act, and is answerable to the legislature through the concerned minister.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Statutory Corporations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Forms of Public Sector Enterprises

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Government Companies' refers to.
questions.a: A government company is a company in which not less than 51 percent of the paid-up share capital is held by the central government, by any state government or governments, or jointly by the central and state governments, and includes a subsidiary of such a government company.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Government Companies'.
questions.a: Government companies are registered under the Companies Act like any private company, but the majority ownership rests with the government, giving it control over management while allowing corporate flexibility.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Government Companies' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Forms of Public Sector Enterprises

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Private Sector Enterprises' refers to.
questions.a: Private sector enterprises are business organisations owned, managed and controlled by private individuals or groups with the primary objective of earning profit, and include sole proprietorships, partnership firms, joint Hindu families, cooperatives and companies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Private Sector Enterprises'.
questions.a: The private sector is driven by the profit motive and individual initiative, and its forms differ in ownership structure, liability, capital-raising capacity and continuity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Private Sector Enterprises' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Private Sector

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Joint Ventures' refers to.
questions.a: A joint venture is a business arrangement where two or more parties, which may be private companies, government companies or foreign companies, pool their resources to undertake a specific project or business activity, sharing the risks, rewards and control as agreed between them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Joint Ventures'.
questions.a: Joint ventures combine the strengths, capital and expertise of the partners while sharing risks, and are especially useful for entering new markets or undertaking large projects.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Joint Ventures' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Forms of Business Organisations

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Multinational Corporations' refers to.
questions.a: A multinational corporation is a company that owns or controls production of goods or services in one or more countries other than its home country, operating through subsidiaries, branches or affiliates across national boundaries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Multinational Corporations'.
questions.a: MNCs have a global vision, huge capital resources, advanced technology and centralised control with decentralised operations, enabling them to exploit economies of scale and international market opportunities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Multinational Corporations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Global Enterprises

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Public Sector versus Private Sector' refers to.
questions.a: The public sector consists of enterprises owned and operated by the government with the objective of public welfare, while the private sector consists of enterprises owned and managed by individuals with the objective of earning profit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Public Sector versus Private Sector'.
questions.a: The two sectors differ in ownership, purpose, capital source, accountability, decision-making freedom and the role of social welfare versus profit.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Public Sector versus Private Sector' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Public and Private Sector Comparison

concepts.title: Changing Role of the Public Sector

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Changing Role of the Public Sector' refers to.
questions.a: The changing role of the public sector refers to the shift in government policy from direct ownership and control of enterprises towards a facilitator role, driven by poor performance, inefficiency and the need to encourage private investment and competition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Changing Role of the Public Sector'.
questions.a: Reforms such as disinvestment, deregulation and greater autonomy aim to improve efficiency, reduce government burden and redefine the public sector's role from a producer to a facilitator of economic activity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Changing Role of the Public Sector' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Public Sector Reforms

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Disinvestment' refers to.
questions.a: Disinvestment is the process of selling or liquidating a part of the government's equity stake in a public sector enterprise to private investors, with the aim of raising resources, improving efficiency and reducing the government's burden of managing such enterprises.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Disinvestment'.
questions.a: Disinvestment transfers part of public ownership to private hands, bringing in private capital and management practices while raising revenue for the government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Disinvestment' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Public Sector Reforms
